items.value: Based on this image: **TATTOO KNOLLING EXTRACTION** Analyze the source image and isolate every visible tattoo as a clean tattoo design reference. Reconstruct the tattoo art as faithfully as possible, even if it is wrapped around skin, partly distorted by perspective, or interrupted by body curvature. **Extraction protocol:** 1. Detect every visible tattoo or tattoo fragment. 2. Identify the body zone for each tattoo from the source context. 3. Visually unwrap the tattoo from skin curvature into a flat readable design. 4. Preserve line weight, ink density, shading, color, negative space, style, symbols, text, aging, scars, and imperfect real-world details. 5. If part of the tattoo is hidden or distorted, reconstruct only what is strongly implied by visible continuity. Do not invent decorative filler. **Knolling board output:** - Neutral matte background. - Each tattoo isolated as a large flat design panel. - Arrange tattoos by body area or visual family. - Use clean spacing, no overlap, no mockup skin texture unless needed to explain placement. - Include tiny unobtrusive labels only if they help identify body zone. - The unfolded tattoo designs are the main subject and should occupy most of the frame. [TATTOO_PLACE_IT_PLACEHOLDER] **Quality lock:** - Faithful to the source tattoo first, aesthetic cleanup second. - Do not redesign the tattoo. - Do not turn the tattoo into generic flash art. - Keep the original tattoo identity, imperfections and proportions.

Based on this image: **KNOLLING OBJECT DECONSTRUCTION** Analyze the object in the image and generate a knolling board displaying all its component parts in a logical, exploded arrangement. **Deconstruction Protocol:** 1. **Identify the object type:** Mechanical, electronic, organic, composite 2. **Determine logical disassembly:** What parts can be separated? 3. **Categorize components:** - Structural elements (frame, body, housing) - Mechanical parts (gears, hinges, fasteners) - Electronic components (if applicable) - Consumable/replaceable parts - Decorative elements **Disassembly Logic:** - Follow actual assembly/disassembly sequence - Group related parts together - Show fasteners near their corresponding parts - Maintain left-to-right or top-to-bottom assembly flow - Smallest components (screws, washers) arranged in neat rows **Knolling Rules:** - Neutral grey background (#d0d0d0) - All parts at strict 90° angles to frame edges - No overlapping — clear separation between all items - Parts cleaned and displayed at optimal viewing angle - Scale preserved — show actual size relationships - Shadow direction consistent (soft, upper-left source) **Output Composition:** - Overhead camera, perpendicular to surface - Main body/housing positioned centrally or upper-left - Components radiate outward in logical groups - Include subtle part-count impression (the satisfaction of seeing everything) - High detail on textures, wear marks, material qualities Generate as a technical flat lay photograph with museum-quality precision.

Based on this image: **KNOLLING SCENE DECONSTRUCTION** Analyze the scene/environment in the image and generate a knolling board displaying all identifiable elements organized into 5 distinct categories. **Scene Analysis Protocol:** 1. **Survey the environment type:** Interior, exterior, urban, rural, industrial, domestic 2. **Identify all discrete elements** that could theoretically be isolated 3. **Assign to exactly 5 categories** (no more, no less) **Category Framework Examples:** FOR EXTERIOR/URBAN SCENES: - Category A: ARCHITECTURE (buildings, structures, facades, doorways) - Category B: STREET FURNITURE (benches, bins, bollards, signage) - Category C: VEHICLES (cars, bikes, any transport) - Category D: INFRASTRUCTURE (poles, wires, road sections, drains) - Category E: NATURE/ORGANIC (trees, plants, birds, sky elements) FOR INTERIOR/DOMESTIC SCENES: - Category A: FURNITURE (major pieces — bed, sofa, table, chairs) - Category B: WALL ELEMENTS (posters, art, mirrors, clocks, switches) - Category C: LIGHTING (lamps, fixtures, candles, windows as light sources) - Category D: TEXTILES (rugs, curtains, cushions, blankets) - Category E: OBJECTS/DECOR (books, plants, ornaments, personal items) **Knolling Rules:** - Neutral background (#c8c8c8) - Image divided into 5 horizontal rows OR 5 labeled zones - Each category clearly separated with visual breathing room - Items within categories arranged at 90° angles - NO overlapping between any elements - Scale adjusted for composition (miniaturized buildings, proportional small items) - Largest/most significant item per category anchors that row **Output Composition:** - Overhead view, flat perspective - Each category row labeled with small, clean typography (optional) - Consistent lighting across all elements - Elements should look like architectural model pieces or props - Total composition fills frame with balanced density Generate as a taxonomic inventory photograph — every element of the scene laid bare.

Based on this image/theme: **KNOLLING BOARD EXPLORER — SEASONAL SHIFTS GRID** **Phase 1: Visual Analysis & Knolling Deconstruction** 1. Identify Core Elements: List all objects, their seasonal appropriateness, material weights. 2. Extract Style DNA: What is the core identity that must survive seasonal adaptation? 3. Map Functional Needs: How does weather change what this person needs? 4. Preserve Recognition: The style must be instantly recognizable across all seasons. **Phase 2: The 3x3 Seasonal Shift Grid** --- **ROW 1 — WINTER SPECTRUM:** 1. **DEEP WINTER (Survival Mode)** Heaviest layering, maximum protection. Swap items for: insulated outerwear, thermal layers, waterproof boots, wool accessories (gloves, scarf, beanie). Colors shift darker, richer. Add: hand warmers, heavy-duty bag, chapstick. Background: cool grey. Texture emphasis on wool, down, rubber, technical fabrics. The "blizzard-ready" version. 2. **HOLIDAY WINTER (Festive)** Winter weight but with celebratory accents. Keep silhouette cozy but add: velvet textures, metallic touches, richer colors (burgundy, forest green, gold). Add objects: gift wrap fragment, invitation card, cocktail napkin. Background: deep green or burgundy. The "office party to family dinner" version. Elevated, intentional, slightly dressy. 3. **LATE WINTER (Thaw Pending)** Transitional. Lighter layers starting to appear under heavy coat. Mix of winter staples and early spring optimism. Add: umbrella, waterproof layer, transitional boots. Colors: grey, navy, emerging pastels. Background: slate grey. Puddle-ready. The "sick of winter but not risking it" version. --- **ROW 2 — SPRING/SUMMER ARC:** 4. **EARLY SPRING (Cautious Emergence)** Layers that can be added/removed. Light jacket over lighter layers. Swap heavy boots for transitional footwear. Colors brighten: soft blues, greens, creams. Add: sunglasses, allergy medication implied, light scarf. Background: soft sage. The "might be warm, might snow" version. Hopeful but prepared. 5. **PEAK SUMMER (Heat Maximum)** Minimum viable coverage. Lightest fabrics, most skin, breathable everything. Swap for: shorts/skirt, sandals or light sneakers, tank or linen shirt. Add: sunscreen, water bottle, sweat-wicking items. Colors: whites, naturals, bright accents. Background: warm cream. The "function over form, survival over style" version. 6. **LATE SUMMER (Golden Hour)** Still warm but richer. Summer items in harvest tones — amber, terracotta, olive, cream. Slightly more coverage returning. Add: light cardigan for evening, warmer accessories. Background: wheat/golden. The "last beach weekend" version. Nostalgic summer, golden light, end-of-season energy. --- **ROW 3 — AUTUMN DESCENT:** 7. **EARLY AUTUMN (Crisp Optimism)** The favorite season version. Perfect layering weather. Swap for: medium-weight jacket, boots return, scarves for style not survival. Colors: rust, burgundy, camel, olive. Add: coffee cup ring stain, fallen leaf. Background: warm taupe. The "finally can wear real clothes" version. Cozy but not heavy. 8. **DEEP AUTUMN (Pre-Winter)** Darker, heavier, preparing for cold. Substantial coat, heavier boots, gloves appearing. Colors deepen: charcoal, brown, deep red. Add: tissues, umbrella, comfort items. Background: dark brown. Rain-ready, wind-resistant. The "denial about winter" version. 9. **EXTREME WEATHER (Climate Event)** Pick a weather extreme and adapt: HEATWAVE (emergency cooling, minimal layers, wet towel), MONSOON (full waterproofing, sealed bags, rain boots), DUST STORM (face coverage, goggles, sealed layers), HUMID TROPICAL (anti-moisture, breathable mesh, moisture-wicking everything). Background matches climate. The "survival" version. --- **Technical Execution:** - All 9 boards maintain same arrangement logic - Object SUBSTITUTION not just color change — different actual items per season - Style DNA must remain recognizable (same subculture/aesthetic, different expression) - Consistent overhead lighting, temperature-appropriate color grading - Final output: 3x3 contact sheet showing full seasonal wardrobe **TO USE:** 1. Provide source image OR describe the base style/knolling 2. Specify if any items are "sacred" (must appear in all seasons) 3. For #9 (Extreme): specify the weather event 4. Indicate geographic context (affects seasonal interpretation)

Based on this image/theme: **KNOLLING BOARD EXPLORER — COLOR MUTATIONS GRID** **Phase 1: Visual Analysis & Knolling Deconstruction** 1. Identify Core Elements: List all objects, original colors, material properties. 2. Extract Color DNA: Dominant hues, accent colors, neutral base, color temperature. 3. Map Material Response: How would each material accept color change? (fabric absorbs, metal reflects, leather patinas) 4. Preserve Recognition: Objects must remain identifiable despite color shift. **Phase 2: The 3x3 Color Mutation Grid** --- **ROW 1 — MONOCHROME STUDIES:** 1. **VOID BLACK (Total Absorption)** Every item rendered in matte black. Different textures create variation — soft black fabric, glossy black leather, rough black metal. Background: pure white for maximum contrast. The silhouette becomes everything. Objects read as shadow-forms, defined only by shape and texture grain. 2. **CLINICAL WHITE (Bleached Clean)** All items in pure white and off-white variants. Cream, ivory, bone, chalk, porcelain. Background: light grey to separate objects. Hospital sterile. Objects feel sanitized, specimens, forensic evidence bags. Texture and form dominate. Ghost version of the original. 3. **SINGLE HUE SPECTRUM (Monochromatic Gradient)** Choose ONE color (specify: red, blue, green, etc.). All items rendered in variations of that single hue — from near-black deep tones to pale tints. Background: complementary neutral. Creates a color study, like a Pantone exploration. Objects unified by hue, differentiated by saturation/value. --- **ROW 2 — PALETTE MANIPULATIONS:** 4. **INVERTED/NEGATIVE** Colors flipped to their photographic negative. Blue becomes orange, red becomes cyan, dark becomes light. Background inverts too. Unsettling, alien, like looking at an X-ray of the style. Objects feel like they're from a parallel dimension. 5. **DESATURATED ARCHIVE (Faded Memory)** Drain 70% saturation from all items. Colors become whispers — pale, dusty, sun-bleached. Add subtle sepia/yellow undertone. Background: warm grey. Objects feel like they've been stored in an attic for decades. The nostalgia filter. Melancholic, distant, remembered rather than present. 6. **OVERSATURATED FEVER (Color Amplified)** Push all colors to maximum saturation. Reds become crimson, blues become electric, greens become toxic. Background: black to make colors pop violently. Objects feel radioactive, synthetic, candy-coated. The fever dream version. Too much, deliberately overwhelming. --- **ROW 3 — MATERIAL TRANSFORMATIONS:** 7. **METALLIC TRANSMUTATION** All items rendered in metallic finishes. Specify: GOLD (warm, luxurious, baroque), SILVER (cold, futuristic, clinical), COPPER (warm, industrial, steampunk), or MIXED (each item different metal). Background: black velvet. Objects become trophies, artifacts, precious relics. The "everything you own, cast in bronze" museum. 8. **NEON CONTAMINATION** Keep original color base but add neon edge-glow and highlights. Fluorescent pink, electric blue, acid green bleeding into natural colors. Background: deep black. Objects look like they're under UV club lighting. Synthetic, nocturnal, cyberpunk residue. 9. **NATURAL DYE SHIFT** Recolor all items using only pigments available from natural dyes — indigo, madder red, turmeric yellow, walnut brown, iron black. Background: raw linen. Colors become earthy, imperfect, handmade-feeling. Objects feel artisanal, pre-industrial, craft-made. The heritage version. --- **Technical Execution:** - All 9 boards maintain identical composition/arrangement - Only COLOR changes — shapes, positions, objects remain constant - Consistent overhead lighting (adjust temperature per variation) - Background color specified per variation - Final output: 3x3 contact sheet showing color progression **TO USE:** 1. Provide source image OR describe the original knolling 2. For #3 (Single Hue): specify the color 3. For #7 (Metallic): specify gold, silver, copper, or mixed 4. Indicate if any specific items should resist color change

[MULTI_IMAGE_PLACEHOLDER]Based on this image: **DECOR EXTRACTION — 360° EQUIRECTANGULAR PANORAMA** Remove ALL human figures. Generate a true EQUIRECTANGULAR projection panorama (NOT fisheye, NOT wide-angle crop). **CHARACTER REMOVAL:** - Remove all people/animals completely - Inpaint with environment from source - Maintain lighting consistency **EQUIRECTANGULAR PROJECTION — TECHNICAL SPEC:** This is a SPECIFIC projection format used for HDRI, VR, and 3D environment maps. **VISUAL CHARACTERISTICS OF EQUIRECTANGULAR:** - Aspect ratio: EXACTLY 2:1 (example: 4096×2048, 8192×4096) - Horizontal lines (tables, horizons) stay STRAIGHT in the middle, curve toward top/bottom - Vertical lines (walls, doors) stay STRAIGHT throughout - Top edge = ceiling directly above camera (zenith) — appears STRETCHED horizontally - Bottom edge = floor directly below camera (nadir) — appears STRETCHED horizontally - Left and right edges = the SAME point in space (seamless wrap) - Objects near top/bottom edges appear horizontally stretched/distorted - Objects at horizon level (middle band) appear most natural **WHAT EQUIRECTANGULAR IS NOT:** - NOT a fisheye (fisheye is circular, equirectangular is rectangular 2:1) - NOT a wide panorama crop (those don't cover full 180° vertical) - NOT a perspective photo with wide lens - NOT curved at the sides like barrel distortion **REFERENCE:** Google "equirectangular projection" or "HDRI environment map" — the output should look exactly like those examples. **SEAMLESS WRAP:** - Left edge and right edge must be IDENTICAL (they represent same point in 360° space) - When wrapped into a sphere, no visible seam - Test: mentally scroll image left-to-right in loop — transition must be invisible **FIDELITY:** - Extend source environment faithfully — don't invent major elements - Match materials, colors, lighting throughout 360° - Keep unseen areas simple if not evidenced in source **COLOR GRADING LOCK:** - EXACT color grade from source across entire panorama - No drift from left to right edge - Clone the grade, no auto-correction **OUTPUT:** - Single image, STRICT 2:1 ratio - High resolution (4K+ width recommended) - NO TEXT/LABELS - Ready for: HDRI lighting, VR viewer, Blender/Unity skybox

Based on this image/theme: **KNOLLING BOARD EXPLORER — 9 VARIATIONS GRID** **Phase 1: Visual Analysis & Knolling Deconstruction** 1. Identify Core Elements: List all objects, categories, materials, colors, era markers. 2. Extract Style DNA: Subculture, aesthetic, era, lifestyle. Signature items vs. supporting details. 3. Map Color Palette: Primary tones, accents, background, material textures. 4. Assess Composition Logic: Arrangement, density, negative space, scale hierarchy. **Phase 2: The 3x3 Knolling Variation Grid** --- **ROW 1 — AUTEUR INTERPRETATIONS:** 1. **WES ANDERSON CURATION** Pastel background (pink, mint, or cream). Symmetry obsessive. Items arranged with mathematical precision. Add whimsical ephemera: vintage postcard, enamel pin, obscure book. Futura Bold label beneath each object. Everything looks like it belongs to a fictional private school or a melancholic European hotel. 2. **DAVID LYNCH EVIDENCE** Black velvet background. Lighting slightly off — too bright in spots, shadow pools elsewhere. Objects feel like they shouldn't be together. Add one inexplicable item (a tooth, a key to nothing, a burned photograph). Something red. Something humming with wrongness. The knolling of a dream you can't quite remember. 3. **HELMUT LANG REDUCTION** Industrial concrete or raw steel background. Strip the selection to monochrome — black, white, grey, bone. Remove all branding, all logos. What remains is sculptural. Negative space dominates. Each object earns its presence through form alone. Cold, austere, untouchable. --- **ROW 2 — MATERIAL & STATE MUTATIONS:** 4. **ENTROPY STUDY (Worn/Destroyed)** Same objects but at the end of their life. Leather cracked, fabric frayed, metal oxidized, paper yellowed. The knolling of a style lived hard. Signs of use, repair, devotion. Objects that have stories embedded in their damage. 5. **ESSENTIAL (Core DNA Only)** Strip everything back to 4-6 objects maximum. Only the irreducible signatures that define the style — if you removed any single item, the identity collapses. No redundancy, no decoration, no "nice to have." Brutal editorial selection. Maximum negative space. Each object is load-bearing. 6. **GORE VERSION (Violence Applied)** Same objects but subjected to physical trauma. Fabric slashed and hanging. Leather punctured. Fresh blood splatter — still wet, viscous, catching light. Burn marks with blackened edges and exposed material beneath. Broken glass. Melted plastic. The violence is recent. Something happened here. Clinical overhead lighting makes it more disturbing — forensic, not cinematic. --- **ROW 3 — NARRATIVE & HYBRID:** 7. **CROSS-POLLINATION (Hybrid)** Merge this style with an unexpected second influence. Specify the collision: Skinhead × Techwear / Mod × Solarpunk / Ivy League × Fetish. 70% original DNA + 30% foreign injection. The objects should create productive tension — familiar but mutated. 8. **NARRATIVE ARTIFACT (Story Evidence)** Add 3-5 objects that imply a specific story — concert ticket stub, handwritten note with phone number, hospital bracelet, stained item, cracked phone screen, polaroid of someone cropped out. The knolling becomes forensic evidence. Prompt: "What happened to this person?" 9. **GEOGRAPHIC TRANSPLANT** Same subculture but different city's interpretation. Specify: TOKYO version (tighter fits, obscure local brands, meticulous), BERLIN version (darker, worn harder, club residue), LAGOS version (bolder patterns, different textiles, local craft meets imported signifiers), MEXICO CITY version (warmer palette, silver jewelry, specific local codes). How does geography mutate a style? --- **Technical Execution:** - All 9 boards use IDENTICAL aspect ratio - Consistent overhead lighting (varies per concept where noted) - Strict 90° knolling arrangement throughout - Final output: 3x3 contact sheet, variation title in corner **TO USE:** 1. Provide source image OR describe style/theme 2. For #7: specify the second style to inject 3. For #8: suggest story tone (romantic, violent, mundane, mysterious) 4. For #9: name the city

Generate a 3×3 grid showing 8 rotation views + 1 overhead camera map. **LOCATION CLEANING — CRITICAL:** - REMOVE all people, pedestrians, crowds completely - REMOVE all vehicles (cars, bikes, scooters, trucks, buses) - REMOVE all temporary objects (trash, signs, market stalls) - INPAINT removed areas with logical environment continuation (pavement, walls, ground) - Result: empty, pristine location — architecture and permanent fixtures only **SKY & LIGHTING REPLACEMENT:** - Replace sky with NEUTRAL OVERCAST grey (flat, even, no sun visible) - Soft diffuse lighting — no harsh shadows, no directional sun - Even ambient illumination from all directions - Shadow behavior: subtle ambient occlusion only, no cast shadows - Color temperature: neutral daylight (~5500K), desaturated **3×3 GRID LAYOUT:** **ROW A — FRONT ARC (0° to 90°):** | A1: 0° | A2: 45° | A3: 90° | **ROW B — REAR ARC (135° to 225°):** | B1: 135° | B2: 180° | B3: 225° | **ROW C — SIDE ARC + MAP (270° to 315° + overhead):** | C1: 270° | C2: 315° | C3: CAMERA MAP | **ROTATION VIEWS (A1 ? C2):** - Camera at FIXED center point of location, eye level (~160cm) - Each view rotates around this center point - 0° = primary/entrance direction from references - Consistent lens/focal length across all 8 views - Horizon line at same height in all panels **PANEL C3 — OVERHEAD CAMERA MAP:** - Bird's eye view / floor plan style diagram of the location - Show location footprint (walls, major features) in simplified form - Mark camera position at CENTER with icon - Draw 8 directional arrows or camera icons showing: - A1 (0°), A2 (45°), A3 (90°) - B1 (135°), B2 (180°), B3 (225°) - C1 (270°), C2 (315°) - Label each direction with its grid reference (A1, A2, etc.) - Clean technical diagram style, black lines on light background **RECONSTRUCTION FIDELITY:** - Cross-reference ALL provided images to ensure accuracy - Architecture, textures, materials must match references exactly - Extend visible elements logically — don't invent major features - Where references overlap, ensure perfect consistency - Scale and proportions must remain constant across all views **FORMAT — CRITICAL:** - 3×3 GRID: 9 panels of IDENTICAL width and height - Visible thin separator lines between panels - Views A1-C2: photorealistic render of cleaned location - View C3: technical diagram/map style - NO TEXT except labels in C3 camera map **CONSISTENCY CHECK:** - Same location in all 8 rotation views - Architectural elements visible from multiple angles MUST match - Ground plane continuous and level - Lighting identical across all views (overcast, diffuse) Empty location, neutral grey sky, 8 rotation views + camera map.

[MULTI_IMAGE_PLACEHOLDER]**360° PANORAMIC RECONSTRUCTION — 3×3 GRID** **METAPHOR:** A photographer stands still at one fixed point, takes a photo [IMG_1]= A1, the REFERENCE), then rotates 45° clockwise in place and shoots again (= A2), and so on for 8 photos total. Camera stays at the same height, perfectly horizontal, throughout. The 8 shots tile a complete 360° panorama around that spot. Panel C3 is a top-down map of the spot. **SOURCE:** The attached reference photo IS panel A1. Panels A2 → C2 show new directions from the SAME exact spot, INVENTED but coherent with the reference's architecture, materials, light, atmosphere. **OUTPUT:** 3×3 grid, 8 photorealistic rotation views + 1 overhead diagram (C3). **GRID — each panel = +45° clockwise yaw from A1:** - A1: REFERENCE (forward) - A2: 45° right of A1 - A3: 90° right (perpendicular right) - B1: 135° (behind-right) - B2: 180° — DIRECTLY OPPOSITE A1, what was BEHIND the photographer. NONE of A1's buildings appear here. - B3: 225° (behind-left) - C1: 270° (perpendicular left) - C2: 315° (45° left of A1) - C3: overhead camera map (diagram only) **CAMERA — IDENTICAL ACROSS A1 → C2:** - Single fixed pivot, never translates, only rotates. - YAW ONLY — horizontal body rotation in place. Lens axis parallel to ground. - Camera perfectly LEVEL. No pitch, no tilt, no roll, no Dutch angle. - FORBIDDEN: aerial, bird's-eye, top-down, drone, high-angle, low-angle, oblique. "45°/90°" refer ONLY to body rotation, NEVER to camera tilt. - Eye level (~160 cm). HFOV ~50°. Horizon locked at identical pixel height in all panels. - Focal length, exposure, white balance, color grading all locked to the reference. **LANDMARK ISOLATION — CRITICAL:** The reference's distinctive elements (most colorful/unique buildings, specific façade colors, dominant foreground mass) appear in A1 ONLY.
